result.title: Ontology-Based Contextual AI Evaluations (OB-CAIE) Methodology
result.summary: The ontology-based contextual AI evaluation (OB-CAIE) methodology was developed to address a lack of scientific rigor that arises from unclear testing coverage, to balance human expertise and automations, and to address a lack of reproducibility of AI evaluation testing environments. OB-CAIE strengthens the current state of AI evaluations by addressing the first step in the scientific method by clearly defining what will be tested. Two ontologies represent the tractable problem space in the OB-CAIE methodology: the Domain-Specific Ontology (DSO) and the Evaluation Process Ontology (EPO). The DSO is the what; the EPO is the how. An OB-CAIE problem space can be used for one or multiple AI evaluations. The OB-CAIE methodology allows for human judgment at specific points, in scientifically grounded ways, and in complex subject areas where human feedback is genuinely irreducible or machine irreplaceable. A key advantage of the OB-CAIE methodology is that failure points can be traced, visualized and analyzed within the canonical OB-CAIE methodology problem space.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 OB-CAIE 方法论，用领域本体（DSO，界定「测什么」）与评测过程本体（EPO，界定「怎么测」）刻画可处理的问题空间，以提升 AI 评测的覆盖清晰度、人机分工与可复现性，并支持失败点的追踪与可视化。
AI.relevance_reason: 本体化的「问题空间 + 过程空间」表述可能为 LVR 的评测设计提供线索：把 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等推理阶段的覆盖、证据调用与人机判断点形式化为可追踪对象，从而定位 latent 推理中的信息坍缩或贡献分配失败；但该文面向通用 AI 评测，未涉及视觉或 latent 推理，需核查其概念能否落到具体推理轨迹分析上。
